scenario.name: Mandiant & Snowflake — UNC5537 Campaign: Infostealer Credential Replay & FROSTBITE (Rapeflake) Exfiltration
scenario.shortSubtitle: Mandiant · Snowflake · CISA · Infostealer Logs · Missing MFA · Rapeflake / DBeaver Bulk SQL Staging
scenario.overview: Imagine a grand city courthouse hall with fluted marble columns, an elevated wooden judge bench, a witness stand, and a brass wax-seal notary stamping desk. Entering the marble courthouse hall during a crowded docket, a forger requests a routine certified copy at the notary clerk’s brass stamping counter. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the court notary clerk's station, then smuggles copied records out past the courtroom marble columns in tiny disguised batches. The court bailiff audits the official notary stamp registry and discovers stamped certificates that were never entered into the judge’s docket book. In this scenario (T1078.004, Mandiant & Snowflake, UNC5537 Campaign: Infostealer Credential Replay & FROSTBITE (Rapeflake) Exfiltration), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: replaying Infostealer-Harvested Credentials, then running the FROSTBITE Utility for Rapid, then staging Multi-GB Tables via COPY INTO @~. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Replaying Infostealer-Harvested Credentials, then Running the FROSTBITE Utility for Rapid, then Staging Multi-GB Tables via COPY INTO @~, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: INFOSTEALER CREDENTIAL REPLAY ON SINGLE-FACTOR TENANT
stages.subtitle: Authenticating to *.snowflakecomputing.com without MFA using Lumma/RedLine stealer logs
stages.description: Entering the marble courthouse hall during a crowded docket, a forger requests a routine certified copy at the notary clerk’s brass stamping counter. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the court notary clerk's station while everyday visitors and the court notary clerk go about their routine. UNC5537 searches millions of historical infostealer malware logs (harvested by RedLine, Vidar, and LummaC2 from contractor laptops infected months or years earlier) for URLs matching *.snowflakecomputing.com, and replays those plaintext credentials from Mullvad VPN exit nodes (198.51.100.44) against the customer’s Snowflake login API (which succeeds whenever the target account has SECOND_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR = NULL and no Snowflake Network Policy restricting logins to corporate IP ranges). Because service accounts like SVC_TABLEAU_ETL were frequently configured with static passwords and exempted from MFA to support legacy BI pipelines, possessing a single unrotated password gave UNC5537 immediate ACCOUNTADMIN or SYSADMIN access. In the documented SNOWFLAKE LOGIN_HISTORY exchange from UNC5537 Extortion Operator to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with RESP EVENT_ID 8841920 (confirming that the SINGLE_FACTOR_LOGIN_SUCCESS request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 FROSTBITE (RAPEFLAKE) AUTOMATED SCHEMA RECONNAISSANCE). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ SINGLE_FACTOR_LOGIN_SUCCESS / ⇠#1 RESP EVENT_ID 8841920) from Node ① (#1 UNC5537 Extortion Operator) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Snowflake ACCOUNT_USAGE & SIEM).

stages.title: FROSTBITE (RAPEFLAKE) AUTOMATED SCHEMA RECONNAISSANCE
stages.subtitle: Enumerating ACCOUNTADMIN privileges, users, and high-row-count customer tables
stages.description: Taking advantage of an unguarded moment at the notary desk, the forger lifts the impression of the courthouse wax seal and stamps a stack of unauthorized passes offline. Here in Step 2 inside the courthouse, the intruder uses borrowed access inside the courthouse to slip closer to the brass courthouse wax-seal press without disturbing the sealed judicial record vault. Immediately after authenticating, the operator runs a custom .NET reconnaissance tool tracked by Mandiant as FROSTBITE (which identifies itself in Snowflake’s CLIENT_APPLICATION_ID telemetry under its internal build name "Rapeflake") to automatically execute SHOW DATABASES, SHOW USERS, SHOW ROLES, and SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES (allowing the attacker to instantly score and prioritize customer tenants that hold hundreds of millions of PII or payment rows). Every SQL query and client driver string in Snowflake is immutably recorded in SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY and SESSIONS, exposing the literal "Rapeflake" and "DBeaver_DBeaverUltimate" application strings. In the documented SNOWFLAKE QUERY_HISTORY exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Snowflake Cloud Auth Gateway, Snowflake Cloud Auth Gateway responds with ALERT ROWS_PRODUCED 412 (confirming that the RAPEFLAKE_SCHEMA_RECON request succeeded on Snowflake Cloud Auth Gateway and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 DBEAVER ULTIMATE BULK STAGE & MULTI-GB EXFILTRATION). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ RAPEFLAKE_SCHEMA_RECON / ⇠#2 ALERT ROWS_PRODUCED 412) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Snowflake Cloud Auth Gateway), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Snowflake ACCOUNT_USAGE & SIEM).

stages.title: DBEAVER ULTIMATE BULK STAGE & MULTI-GB EXFILTRATION
stages.subtitle: Executing COPY INTO temporary stages and downloading compressed CSV/Parquet archives
stages.description: Every forged document now bears the court’s own authentic wax emblem, letting the holder command authority in any neighboring municipal hall. In this final step inside the courthouse, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the courtroom marble columns in tiny disguised batches until the court bailiff stamp registry catches the mismatch. To extract tens of millions of rows without timing out, the operator connects via DBeaver Ultimate (using the official Snowflake JDBC driver) and executes COPY INTO @~/dump/customers.csv.gz FROM PROD_DB.PUBLIC.CUSTOMERS (compressing the entire table into GZip CSV chunks inside the user’s personal internal Snowflake stage @~ so they can be rapidly downloaded with the GET command over HTTPS). Staging data into an internal user stage (@~) or temporary stage via COPY INTO leverages Snowflake’s parallel virtual warehouse compute to dump gigabytes of records in seconds. In the documented SNOWFLAKE COPY_INTO exchange from Snowflake Cloud Auth Gateway to FROSTBITE (Rapeflake) Recon Engine, FROSTBITE (Rapeflake) Recon Engine responds with RESP BYTES_WRITTEN 4.8 GB (confirming that the BULK_STAGE_EXFILTRATION request succeeded on FROSTBITE (Rapeflake) Recon Engine and completing the final execution objective of Mandiant & Snowflake, UNC5537 Campaign: Infostealer Credential Replay & FROSTBITE (Rapeflake) Exfiltration). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ BULK_STAGE_EXFILTRATION / ⇠#3 RESP BYTES_WRITTEN 4.8 GB) from Node ③ (#3 Snowflake Cloud Auth Gateway) to Node ④ (#4 FROSTBITE (Rapeflake) Recon Engine), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Snowflake ACCOUNT_USAGE & SIEM).

detectionRule.title: Snowflake Single-Factor Login from Untrusted ASN / DBeaver Client
detectionRule.ruleCode: SELECT * FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY WHERE IS_SUCCESS = 'YES' AND SECOND_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR IS NULL;
detectionRule.mitigation: Enforce MFA (EXT_AUTHN_DUO / SAML2) and attach a strict Snowflake NETWORK_POLICY to all human and service accounts.

detectionRule.title: Mandiant UNC5537 FROSTBITE / Rapeflake Client Application Signature
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: UNC5537 Snowflake Rapeflake or DBeaver Reconnaissance
logsource:
  product: snowflake
detection:
  selection:
    CLIENT_ENVIRONMENT.APPLICATION|contains:
      - 'Rapeflake'
      - 'DBeaver_DBeaverUltimate'
  condition: selection
detectionRule.mitigation: Rotate compromised credentials immediately, terminate active sessions via SYSTEM$ABORT_SESSION, and block non-approved JDBC client identifiers.

detectionRule.title: Anomalous Snowflake Bulk COPY INTO Internal Stage Followed by GET
detectionRule.ruleCode: SELECT USER_NAME, QUERY_TEXT, BYTES_WRITTEN_TO_RESULT FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY WHERE QUERY_TYPE IN ('COPY', 'GET') AND BYTES_WRITTEN_TO_RESULT > 500000000;
detectionRule.mitigation: Restrict CREATE STAGE / COPY INTO privileges and migrate service accounts to Key-Pair Authentication or OAuth Workload Identity.
